searchText: Not sure if given the attack (and assuming a builder has that power, which seems unlikely), this would solve it tho? The idea of the attack is that the builder splits the network such that the validators that get the right payload will get it 'too late' so that the proposer does not have time to retrieve it before proposing, and it will build on EMPTY. Would this change solve this? I'm writing the proofs given the assumption I wrote above (which should reflect what Potuz mentioned) Because the attesters will forward it to the proposer and the proposer would actually accept it. Vs. current gossip rule says you can only accept the first payload you have received. But ya if this goes after second 0 of new slot then it is "too late" Yes exactly that is my understanding of the attack. But probably this addition is worth adding nevertheless? Do you know how is ExecutionPayloadEnvelopesByRoot used? I thought that this could be used to retrieve more payloads in case the one you received was invalid its for short range recovery.. examples... - attestation pointing there's a full block, but i have not seen its payload.. - block building on top of full, but i cant sync the block because i dont have the payload i dont think we have coded behavior that we assume a peer is malicious in a way and try to recover from an invalid payload. It's an interesting thought tho, and doable <@363800010518822915> Beacon-block gossip already IGNOREs + "MAY queue" a block whose parent execution payload hasn't been seen/retrieved. But `on_block` asserts the stronger `is_payload_verified(block.parent_root)` (parent in store.payloads), with no queue note. Can a block pass gossip (parent seen) yet hit the `on_block` assert because the parent isn't verified yet, and get dropped — then stay dropped even after the parent later lands in store.payloads, since nothing re-runs `on_block`? That would cost an honest block its votes and open a reorg. Or does the gossip queue guarantee `on_block` only runs once the parent is verified?

<@363800010518822915> Beacon-block gossip already IGNOREs + "MAY queue" a block whose parent execution payload hasn't been seen/retrieved.

But `on_block` asserts the stronger `is_payload_verified(block.parent_root)` (parent in store.payloads), with no queue note.

Can a block pass gossip (parent seen) yet hit the `on_block` assert because the parent isn't verified yet, and get dropped — then stay dropped even after the parent later lands in store.payloads, since nothing re-runs `on_block`? That would cost an honest block its votes and open a reorg. Or does the gossip queue guarantee `on_block` only runs once the parent is verified?
